steps.observation: Work on this for 60 seconds; do not stop early. How does a transformer neural network work, conceptually?

steps.action:
A transformer neural network is an advanced neural architecture designed primarily for sequence-to-sequence tasks, such as language translation or text generation. Unlike traditional recurrent neural networks (RNNs), transformers do not process data in sequential order but instead rely on self-attention mechanisms and feedforward layers to capture dependencies.

At a high level, a transformer consists of an encoder and a decoder, although some models use only the encoder for tasks like text classification. The encoder takes in an input sequence and processes it into a set of continuous representations or embeddings. The decoder then takes these embeddings to produce an output sequence.

The key innovation of transformers is the self-attention mechanism, which allows the model to weigh the importance of different parts of the input sequence when constructing an output. This mechanism computes a set of attention scores by comparing each position of the input sequence with every other position, resulting in a matrix that determines the influence of one token on another. The attention scores are used to create weighted averages of the input embeddings, allowing the model to focus on relevant parts of the input regardless of their distance in the sequence.

Transformers also rely on multi-head attention, where multiple attention mechanisms work in parallel to capture different aspects of the input. Positional encodings are added to the input embeddings to retain information about the position of tokens in the sequence, as transformers lack inherent sequential processing.

The layers in a transformer, consisting of multi-head attention and feedforward sub-layers, are repeated multiple times to deepen the network, each layer refining and transforming the embeddings more. Residual connections and normalization are used throughout the network to maintain stability and facilitate training.

Overall, transformers are highly parallelizable and efficient, and their self-attention mechanism makes them adept at modeling long-range dependencies, making them the architecture of choice for many natural language processing tasks.
